raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A `--custom-weight-loader` used with `update_weights_from_tensor` sometimes receives an update it cannot apply: a tensor for a parameter it keeps frozen, or the same tensor twice in one session. Today the loader has no way to refuse. Any exception it raises propagates out of `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor`, through the scheduler's request dispatcher (which does not catch handler exceptions), and stops the scheduler. The server goes down and every in-flight request is lost.

Measured on upstream main (`8d4e1ce4c7`): a custom loader that raises `ValueError` during `update_weights_from_tensor` logs `Scheduler hit an exception: ... ValueError`, the scheduler sends SIGQUIT and the whole engine process is killed (1x H100).

## Modifications

- `model_loader/utils.py`: new `WeightUpdateRejected(ValueError)`. A custom loader raises it before it writes any weight.
- `WeightUpdater.update_weights_from_tensor`: a custom loader that raises `WeightUpdateRejected` makes the call return `success=False` with `"<load_format> rejected the update: <message>"`. The scheduler does not advance the weight version, skips the cache flush if no runner on any rank applied the update, and keeps serving. The weight-update session stays open. Any other exception from a custom loader propagates as before.
- Scheduler `update_weights_from_tensor`: like `update_weights_from_ipc` and `update_weights_from_disk`, it now flushes the cache when the target runner applied the update even if a draft runner rejected it afterwards, so a partial update is never served from stale cache.
- Scheduler `update_weights_from_tensor`: the outcome is all-reduced over the tensor-parallel CPU group, so a loader that rejects on some ranks only fails the call on every rank, and every rank flushes its cache if any rank applied the update.
- `docs/docs/advanced_features/sglang_for_rl.mdx`: one note under "Update Weights from Tensor", including the limits: a rejection on any rank fails the call everywhere; the weights stay unchanged only if no rank and no earlier runner applied the update, otherwise the applied weights stay and the cache is flushed.
- New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_weight_update_custom_loader_reject.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`): a rejecting loader returns `(False, message)` and leaves the weights untouched; another exception still propagates.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_weight_version_tracking.py`: a draft rejecting after the target, and a rejection on another tensor-parallel rank, both fail the call, record no version and still flush the cache.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change on any path. A rejected update leaves the weights as they were (TP1 runs on 1x H100 and 1x GB200; the rank-dependent case on 2x GB200):

Engine `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `--enable-deterministic-inference`, 1x H100 80GB, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`. Greedy outputs of 3 prompts (16 tokens) before and after one `update_weights_from_tensor` whose custom loader raises:

| loader raises | upstream main 8d4e1ce4c7 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueError` | scheduler exception, engine killed (SIGQUIT) | same (unchanged by design) |
| `WeightUpdateRejected` | n/a | `success=False`, `"reject_loader.reject_clean rejected the update: ..."`; engine keeps serving; outputs after == before (3/3 token-identical) |
| `WeightUpdateRejected` on tensor-parallel rank 1 only (TP2, 1x GB200 node) | n/a | both ranks return `success=False` ("The update was rejected on another tensor-parallel rank."); engine keeps serving; outputs after == before (3/3) |

Unit tests: `test_weight_update_custom_loader_reject.py` 2/2 and the existing `test_weight_update_tensor_rank.py` 1/1 pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact: one `try` around the custom-loader call.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). No output or speed change; see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

 **Note:** The serialized tensor payloads must be created with `MultiprocessingSerializer.serialize(...)` and should be base64-safe strings.
 
+**Note:** A custom loader (`--custom-weight-loader`) can refuse an update by raising `sglang.srt.model_loader.utils.WeightUpdateRejected` before it writes any weight. The call then returns `success: false` with the loader's message and the server keeps serving. A rejection on any tensor-parallel rank fails the call on every rank. The weights stay unchanged only if no rank and no earlier runner applied the update: where it was applied (another rank's loader accepted, or the target model accepted before the draft model rejected), the new weights stay and the cache is flushed as for a successful update, but the weight version is not advanced. Any other exception raised by a custom loader is not caught.
+
 **Python Engine API:** `engine.update_weights_from_tensor(named_tensors, load_format=None, flush_cache=True)`, inside `begin_weight_update()` / `end_weight_update()`.
 
 ### Update Weights from Distributed Group

@@ -242,18 +242,40 @@ def update_weights_from_tensor(self, recv_req: UpdateWeightsFromTensorReqInput):
                 recv_req.serialized_named_tensors
             )
             success, message = True, "Success"
-            for _, runner in self._select_runners(recv_req.selector):
+            target_updated = False

+            # on the result so that every rank reports the same outcome and
+            # flushes the cache if any rank applied the update.
+            if (
+                self.tp_cpu_group is not None
+                and torch.distributed.get_world_size(group=self.tp_cpu_group) > 1

@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+"""A custom weight loader refuses a tensor update by raising WeightUpdateRejected."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner_components.weight_updater import (
+    WeightUpdater,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_loader.utils import WeightUpdateRejected
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=9, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_MODULE = "sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner_components.weight_updater"
+_LOADER = "my_pkg.loaders.load"
+
+
+def _reject(model, named_tensors):
+    raise WeightUpdateRejected("layer 3 is frozen")
+
+
+def _crash(model, named_tensors):
+    raise RuntimeError("loader bug")
+
+
+class TestCustomLoaderReject(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.model = torch.nn.Linear(2, 2, bias=False)
+        self.original = self.model.weight.detach().clone()
+        self.updater = WeightUpdater(
+            tp_rank=0,
+            device="cpu",
+            gpu_id=0,
+            model_config=None,
+            custom_weight_loaders=[_LOADER],
+            get_model=lambda: self.model,
+            update_model_fields=lambda *args, **kwargs: None,
+            recapture_cuda_graph=lambda: None,
+            get_model_runner=lambda: None,
+        )
+
+    def _update(self, loader):
+        # monkey_patch_torch_reductions() would patch torch's tensor pickling
+        # for the rest of the process; the plain tensors here do not need it.
+        with (
+            patch(f"{_MODULE}.monkey_patch_torch_reductions"),
+            patch(f"{_MODULE}.dynamic_import", return_value=loader),
+            patch(
+                f"{_MODULE}.get_model",
+                return_value=SimpleNamespace(weight_cache_mode="off"),
+            ),
+            get_parallel().override(tp_rank=0),
+        ):
+            return self.updater.update_weights_from_tensor(
+                [("weight", torch.zeros(2, 2))], load_format=_LOADER
+            )
+
+    def test_rejected_update_returns_failure(self):
+        success, message = self._update(_reject)
+        self.assertFalse(success)
+        self.assertIn(_LOADER, message)
+        self.assertIn("layer 3 is frozen", message)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(self.model.weight.detach(), self.original))
+
+    def test_other_loader_errors_propagate(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            self._update(_crash)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
